key_insight: Better reliability diagnostics do not necessarily improve materials screening decisions or reduce DFT verification costs.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate reliability interventions by how much DFT they avoid while preserving required recall of near-hull candidates, rather than by prediction metrics alone.
method: Rank candidate crystal structures with MACE-MP, CHGNet, and Orb V3 before DFT verification.
Test novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits against the screening objective.
Use two-oracle analysis to distinguish misaligned reliability targets from finite-budget audit limitations.
evidence_signal: Across the three interventions, improvements in immediate diagnostic targets did not consistently translate into better downstream screening decisions.
watch_item: Routing benefits depend on the screening objective: perfect average-ranking information can still select the wrong model under formation-energy screening, while finite-budget audits limit gains in the evaluated hull-aligned variant.
paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
